handoff.purpose: Define constants, helper functions, and start of temporal_ceiling for measuring co-change ceiling on missed labels.

symbols.name: CLASSES
symbols.note: Tuple of four classification strings: REACHABLE, UNREACHABLE, STATIC_EDGE, NO_INSCOPE_DEF.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_SHARE
symbols.note: Minimum share of scored labels to trigger reopen signal, set to 0.10.

symbols.name: REOPEN_MIN_TASKS
symbols.note: Minimum distinct tasks to trigger reopen signal, set to 3.

symbols.name: _symbol_defs
symbols.note: Returns dict mapping symbol names to set of in-scope rels defining that symbol, from current worktree.

symbols.name: _parents_of
symbols.note: Returns list of parent SHAs for a given commit SHA, or None on failure.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver
symbols.note: Resolves historical aliases for file paths via git log --follow, with caching.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes resolver with repo path, timeout, failure counter, and empty cache.

symbols.name: _AliasResolver.aliases
symbols.effects_note: Runs git log --follow subprocess on cache miss.
symbols.note: Returns set of historical aliases for a given relative path at a given revision.

symbols.name: _partner_counts
symbols.note: Returns dict mapping partner spelling to co-change count against any alias of the focus.

symbols.name: _classify
symbols.note: Classifies each missed label into one of four categories based on static edges and co-change counts.

symbols.name: temporal_ceiling
symbols.note: Computes both arms of the ceiling over miss tasks; returns dict. Read-only.

claims.text: Read-only: never writes the store, the baseline, or any file.
claims.why: No file writes or side effects visible in this chunk; all functions are read-only.

claims.text: Imports only structcore's stable public API plus sibling eval modules.
claims.why: Imports from daedalus.structcore and .harness, .tasks; no other external imports.

claims.text: The clean arm therefore computes pairs over ``git log <minted_at_sha>^`` -- history strictly before the mint (first-parent semantics; merge SHAs are flagged in the row rather than silently half-counted).
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the logic for flagging merge SHAs; only computes rev = f'{sha}^' if has_rev else None. Merge flagging is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: The LEAKY arm (full history) is computed alongside on purpose
claims.why: temporal_ceiling computes both clean_pairs (with rev) and leaky_pairs (without rev).

claims.text: RENAME-AWARE, BECAUSE THE ADVERSARIAL PASS PROVED IT MATTERS.
claims.why: The _AliasResolver class resolves historical aliases via git log --follow, and _partner_counts sums counts across spellings before thresholding.

claims.text: This module resolves every focus/defining file to its full historical alias set (``git log --follow``) and sums co-change counts across spellings BEFORE applying ``min_count``.
claims.why: temporal_ceiling calls aliases.aliases() to get focus aliases, and _partner_counts sums counts across spellings; min_count is applied later in _classify.

claims.text: The first version of this check was rename-blind and published "rename-aware matching does not change it" -- the adversarial review (Nemesis, 2026-07-21) refuted exactly that sentence by hand-verifying a real verifier.py<->providers/ollama.py coupling across the rebrand boundary.
claims.why: Historical claim about prior version; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: MEASURED CLOSE (2026-07-21, agent_env corpus, 7 miss tasks / 43 missed labels; rename-blind first pass corrected by the Nemesis rename-map recount, then reproduced by this module): clean ceiling at min_count=2 = 1/43 = 2.3% (a single label, ``_dispatch``: genuine verifier<->ollama coupling crossing the rebrand); min_count=1 adds nothing further; leaky full-history arm = 6/43 at min_count=2 and 42/43 at min_count=1
claims.why: Historical measurement results; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: Structural context that bounds any future hope here: 41 of 43 missed labels sit on focus files BORN AT THEIR MINT COMMIT (zero pre-mint history -- test files created by the very feature commit they were minted from), so for them clean unreachability is structural truth under ANY enrichment; the remaining NO_INSCOPE_DEF label (``_py_maps``) is a stale label whose definition the mint commit itself deleted.
claims.why: Claims about specific corpus statistics; not verifiable from this code.

claims.text: THE REOPEN CONDITION (with a materiality floor -- a lone recoverable label must not reopen a core-API build): reopen the enrichment lane only when a re-run on a grown corpus reports a clean, rename-aware ceiling at min_count >= 2 that clears ``REOPEN_MIN_SHARE`` of scored labels OR touches ``REOPEN_MIN_TASKS`` distinct tasks.
claims.why: The reopen logic is not implemented in this chunk; only constants are defined.

claims.text: Caveat to carry: a corpus whose focus files are born at their mint commits (like today's) can NEVER trip this regardless of how real temporal coupling is elsewhere -- the zero generalizes weakly, so re-run it as the corpus grows rather than citing today's close as permanent.
claims.why: Speculative claim about future behaviour; not verifiable from code.

observations.what: Module docstring contains extensive historical context and design rationale, but no functional code beyond imports and constants.
_parents_of returns None on subprocess error; callers must handle None. In temporal_ceiling, parents is checked with bool(parents) so None leads to has_rev=False, which is safe.
observations.where: _parents_of function and its usage in temporal_ceiling

observations.what: _AliasResolver.aliases uses a cache with key (rev, rel). Cache includes None rev. Docstring says degrades to {rel} on failure, which matches code.
_partner_counts expects pairs from co_change_pairs(min_count=1). If called with different min_count, the thresholding logic may be incorrect. Not checkable if this invariant is enforced elsewhere.
_classify uses def_count callable which is not defined in this chunk; its behaviour is unknown. The classification logic depends on that callable.
temporal_ceiling calls eval_task_tier1 from .harness; its implementation is not in this chunk. The row structure and error handling depend on that function.
temporal_ceiling uses 'import_edges' and 'import_edges_reverse' from idx, defaulting to empty dict if missing. This is robust.
The chunk ends mid-function; the rest of temporal_ceiling and other functions are in chunk 2.
